title: The Natural System expresses propinquity of descent

fields.label: Label
fields.value: The Natural System expresses propinquity of descent

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The 'something more' than mere resemblance that naturalists seek in the Natural System is closeness of descent, which is the only known cause of similarity among organisms and is partially revealed by classifications.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: propinquity of descent,—the only known cause of the similarity of organic beings,—is the bond, hidden as it is by various degrees of modification, which is partially revealed to us by our classifications.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter XIII, “Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs”; section “Natural system”. Scope: biological classification of all organisms

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch13-02: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.68

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The correspondence between classification and descent is testable using independent evidence. The uniqueness and conceptual identity claims cannot be fully adjudicated by datasets.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare independently inferred molecular phylogenetic distances with historical and modern classifications and organismal similarity matrices. Stronger agreement with common descent than with non-genealogical similarity schemes supports the empirical content, but cannot establish the philosophical phrase 'only known cause.'

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Modern classifications often already incorporate phylogenies, creating circularity.

The 'Natural System' and 'something more' are partly conceptual.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Congruence between molecular trees and named groups is a real empirical core, and the needed trees and classifications are public. The wording also makes a conceptual claim about the hidden bond of the Natural System and about descent as the only cause of similarity, which those databases do not settle. The feasible analysis therefore tests a proxy, phylogenetic concordance, rather than the claim in full.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare traditional classifications with independently estimated molecular trees and ask whether closeness of descent predicts classificatory grouping beyond raw similarity. The claim is confirmed if classifications recover phylogenetic proximity after phenotypic similarity is accounted for, and refuted if they track overall resemblance or ecological similarity instead.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Gene transfer and convergence also generate similarity, so descent is not the only measurable cause.

Many ranks were revised after molecular trees existed, so congruence with those trees is partly by later construction.

What naturalists 'seek' in a natural system is a historical intention, not a column in a dataset.
